en: Saṃyutta Nikāya 29.1 Nāgavagga Suddhikasutta At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. What four? The person who is like a nāga; the person who is like a lion; the person who is like a ram; and the person who is like a jackal. And how, bhikkhus, is one a person like a nāga? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is virtuous, restrained with the restraint of the Pātimokkha, perfect in conduct and resort, and seeing fear in the slightest fault, he trains by undertaking the training rules. This is called a person like a nāga. And how, bhikkhus, is one a person like a lion? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells as one who has attained the destruction of the taints in this very life, having realized for himself with direct knowledge that state which is taintless, liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, having reached it right here and now. This is called a person like a lion. And how, bhikkhus, is one a person like a ram? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is a mere repeater of the Dhamma, one who repeats the Dhamma as he has heard it and learned it from others. This is called a person like a ram. And how, bhikkhus, is one a person like a jackal? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is a maker of strife, a creator of quarrels, a rouser of disputes, a maker of issues, one who lives devoted to accusations and litigation. This is called a person like a jackal. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world.”
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
"Bhikkhus, there are these four wombs of nāgas.
Which four?"
“Bhikkhus, there are these four modes of birth for nāgas: nāgas born from eggs, nāgas born from a womb, nāgas born from moisture, and nāgas born spontaneously.
These, bhikkhus, are the four modes of birth for nāgas.
The first.

Saṃyutta Nikāya 29.2 (SN 29.2, PTS SN iii 240) 1. Nāgavagga Paṇītatarasutta — The Discourse on the More Excellent “Monks, there are these four kinds of nāgas. What four? The nāga that is bound by a chain; the nāga that is bound by a rope; the nāga that is bound by a goad; and the nāga that is bound by a jewel. These, monks, are the four kinds of nāgas. Of these four kinds of nāgas, monks, which one is the most excellent? “It is the nāga that is bound by a jewel, venerable sir. “Monks, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One is like the nāga that is bound by a jewel. Why is that? Just as, monks, the nāga that is bound by a jewel is not bound by a chain, nor by a rope, nor by a goad, so too, monks, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One is not bound by sensual pleasures, nor by ill will, nor by harmfulness. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One is like the nāga that is bound by a jewel.”
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
"Bhikkhus, there are these four wombs of nāgas.
Which four?"
There are egg-born nāgas, womb-born nāgas, moisture-born nāgas, and spontaneously born nāgas.
Among these, monks, the womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously born nāgas are more excellent than the egg-born nāgas.
Among these, monks, the moisture-born and spontaneously born nāgas are more excellent than both the egg-born and womb-born nāgas.
In this regard, monks, among the egg-born, the womb-born, and the moisture-born nāgas, the spontaneously born nāgas are more excellent.
These, monks, are the four modes of birth for nāgas. Thus ends the second discourse.

Saṃyutta Nikāya 29.3 (SN 29.3, PTS SN iii 241) 1. The Chapter on Nāgas The Uposatha Sutta At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of nāgas. What four? The nāga who is bound by a bond, yet is not released from the bond; the nāga who is bound by a bond, yet is released from the bond; the nāga who is not bound by a bond, yet is not released from the bond; and the nāga who is not bound by a bond and is released from the bond. And how, bhikkhus, is a nāga bound by a bond and not released from the bond? Here, bhikkhus, a nāga is not free from lust, not free from hatred, not free from delusion regarding the past, the future, and the present. This, bhikkhus, is called a nāga who is bound by a bond and is not released from the bond. And how, bhikkhus, is a nāga bound by a bond and released from the bond? Here, bhikkhus, a nāga is not free from lust, not free from hatred, not free from delusion regarding the past, the future, and the present. This, bhikkhus, is called a nāga who is bound by a bond and released from the bond. And how, bhikkhus, is a nāga not bound by a bond and not released from the bond? Here, bhikkhus, a nāga is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion regarding the past, the future, and the present. This, bhikkhus, is called a nāga who is not bound by a bond and not released from the bond. And how, bhikkhus, is a nāga not bound by a bond and released from the bond? Here, bhikkhus, a nāga is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion regarding the past, the future, and the present. This, bhikkhus, is called a nāga who is not bound by a bond and released from the bond. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of nāgas. Just as, bhikkhus, among quadrupeds the elephant is declared to be the chief, so too, among the ascetics and brahmins of this world, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One is declared to be the chief. Just as, bhikkhus, among quadrupeds the elephant is declared to be the chief, so too, among the ascetics and brahmins of this world, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One is declared to be the chief. For what reason? Because he is not bound by a bond and is released from the bond. This is what the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, further said this: “Bound by a bond, not released from the bond, Bound by a bond, released from the bond, Not bound by a bond, not released from the bond, Not bound by a bond, released from the bond. Among the ascetics and brahmins of this world, Among gods and humans, The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One— He is declared to be the chief.”
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One; having approached, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason why some egg-born nāgas here observe the Uposatha and relinquish their bodies?”
“Here, bhikkhu, it occurs to certain egg-born nāgas:
‘In the past, we were performers of dual conduct by way of body, performers of dual conduct by way of speech, and performers of dual conduct by way of mind.
Having been performers of dual conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, with the breakup of the body, after death, we have been reborn in companionship with egg-born nāgas.’”

"Today let us practice good conduct with the body, let us practice good conduct with speech, and let us practice good conduct with the mind; thus, with the breakup of the body after death, we might be reborn in a happy destination, a heavenly world.
Come now, let us at this very time practice good conduct with the body, let us practice good conduct with speech, and let us practice good conduct with the mind.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the reason why some egg-born *nāgas* observe the Uposatha and relinquish their bodies.
Third.

Saṁyutta Nikāya 29.6 (SN 29.6, PTS SN iii 242) 1.
The Chapter on Nāgas (Nāgavagga)
The Fourth Uposatha Discourse.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why some of these spontaneously born *nāgas* observe the Uposatha and relinquish their bodies?
“Bhikkhu, here it occurs to some spontaneously born *nāgas*:
‘In the past, we were double-dealing in body, double-dealing in speech, and double-dealing in mind.’”

"Since we have acted dualistically in body, dualistically in speech, and dualistically in mind, at the breaking up of the body, after death, we have been reborn in the company of spontaneously born *nāgas*.

If today we were to practice good conduct with the body, good conduct with speech, and good conduct with the mind, then at the breaking up of the body, after death, we would be reborn in a happy destination, a heavenly world.
Come now, let us practice good conduct with the body, good conduct with speech, and good conduct with the mind."
“This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the reason why some spontaneously born nāgas here observe the Uposatha and relinquish their bodies.
The sixth.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 29.7 (SN 29.7, PTS SN iii 243)
1. The Chapter on Nāgas.
Discourse on What is Heard.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born nāgas?
“Here, bhikkhu, someone acts in two ways by way of body, acts in two ways by way of speech, and acts in two ways by way of mind.”
He has heard:
“The egg-born nāgas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that upon the dissolution of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of egg-born nāgas!
He, upon the dissolution of the body, after death, arises in the company of egg-born nāgas.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, upon the dissolution of the body, after death, arises in the company of egg-born nāgas.”
The Seventh.

Saṁyutta Nikāya 29.10 (SN 29.10, PTS SN iii 244) 1.
The Chapter on Nāgas (Nāgavagga)
The Fourth Discourse on What is Heard.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of spontaneously born *nāgas*?
“Bhikkhu, here someone acts in two ways by way of body, acts in two ways by way of speech, and acts in two ways by way of mind.
He has heard:”
“Spontaneously born nāgas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
“Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of spontaneously born nāgas!”
Thus, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the company of spontaneously born nāgas.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of spontaneously born nāgas.
The tenth.

Saṃyutta Nikāya 29.11–20 (SN 29.11, PTS SN iii 244) 1. Nāgavagga The Decad on the Benefit of Giving Eggs (1) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Eggs (2) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Embryos (3) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Fetuses (4) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Infants (5) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Children (6) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Daughters (7) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Sons (8) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Wives (9) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Slaves (10) The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Various Things [In each of these discourses, the Buddha addresses a group of nāgas, explaining that by giving such things as eggs, embryos, fetuses, infants, children, daughters, sons, wives, slaves, and various other goods to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha, one gains great merit and benefits. ... [The text continues with the same structure for each of the ten items listed above. ... Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, suppose a nāga were to give a gift of eggs to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha. By doing so, he would acquire a great deal of merit. Suppose he were to give a gift of embryos... fetuses... infants... children... daughters... sons... wives... slaves... or various other things to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha. By doing so, he would acquire a great deal of merit. [The Buddha repeats this formula for each of the ten items. “This, bhikkhus, is how a nāga gives a gift that is beneficial. [The text concludes with the standard closing formula: This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. (The same structure is repeated for each of the ten suttas, from 11 to 20.)
Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born nāgas?
“Here, bhikkhu, someone acts in two ways by way of body, acts in two ways by way of speech, and acts in two ways by way of mind.”
He has heard:
"The egg-born nāgas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of egg-born nāgas!
He gives food.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of egg-born nāgas.
“This, bhikkhu, is the cause … [as before] … whereby one is reborn … He gives food … he gives clothing …” and so forth.
He gives a vehicle …pe… he gives a garland …pe… he gives perfume …pe…
He gives ointment … [and so on] … he gives a bed … [and so on] … he gives a dwelling … [and so on].
“He gives a lamp.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of egg-born nāgas.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born nāgas.”
The Twentieth [Chapter].
Saṃyutta Nikāya 29.21–50 (SN 29.21, PTS SN iii 245) 1.
The Chapter on Nāgas (Nāgavagga)
The Thirty-two Discourses on Beneficial Gifts, beginning with the Gift of Water and Lilies.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death,
is reborn in the company of nāgas born from eggs … [or] born from moisture … [or] born by spontaneous generation?”
“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person acts dualistically with the body, acts dualistically with speech, and acts dualistically with the mind.
He has heard:
‘The spontaneously born nāgas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’”
It occurs to him:
“Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the spontaneously born *nāgas*!
He gives food... [and so on].
He gives a drink … [and so on] … he gives lighting.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of spontaneously born nāgas.
“This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of spontaneously born *nāgas*.
(By means of this formula, ten suttas each should be composed.
Thus, there are forty explanations regarding the four modes of birth.)
Together with the first ten discourses, there are fifty discourses.
The First Chapter on the Elephant.
Its summary:
The pure, the more excellent,
the four Uposatha days;
what he has heard, and the four.
The gift, the benefit, and the thirty-two [factors];
fifty suttas in total—
thus they are well-expounded in the Nāga [Vagga].
The Connected Discourses on Nāgas are complete.
